ops.expect: ChenMed physicians see 8 to 10 patients per day

set.body: ChenMed operates primary care centers designed for older, lower-income Medicare Advantage patients with complex chronic illness. Its model inverts the usual primary care formula: physicians carry small patient panels, see patients far more often, and spend more face-to-face time with them, supported by on-site care teams and transportation to appointments.
set.outcome: In a matched comparison of 5,695 patients from each model, ChenMed's 'high-touch' patients averaged 8.7 primary care visits a year versus 3.8 under standard care, had 50% fewer hospital admissions, and cost 28% less. The study was led by ChenMed clinicians with University of Miami co-investigators, so it is not independent.
set.source: Ghany R et al., 'High-Touch Care Leads to Better Outcomes and Lower Costs in a Senior Population,' American Journal of Managed Care, September 2018

ops.claim: ChenMed: 8-10 patients/day, 40-minute visits, monthly wellness visits; 30-40% fewer hospitalizations (Health Affairs, 2020)
ops.sources: Ghany R et al., Am J Manag Care, September 2018 (AJMC press release 'Increasing Patient Contact With Doctors Cut Medicare Advantage Costs 28 Percent'): 8.7 vs 3.8 PCP visits/yr, 50% fewer admissions, 28% lower cost, 5,695 matched patients
ops.note: No Health Affairs 2020 study found; visit-length specifics unverifiable; replaced with the real AJMC study and its conflict of interest noted.

ops.expect: every patient discharged is followed by a registered nurse for 30 days

set.body: Copley Hospital is a 25-bed critical access hospital in Morrisville serving a largely rural population. In its 2018 community health needs assessment progress report, filed with the Green Mountain Care Board, Copley described two concrete steps to cut 30-day all-cause readmissions: arranging follow-up with a primary care provider within 7 days of discharge, and reviewing each inpatient readmission in real time to find what went wrong.
set.outcome: Copley reported 30-day all-cause readmission rates of 4.4%–17.0% across January–September 2017 (Vermont critical access hospitals: 8.7%–16.8%) and 6.92% for January–April 2018 — below or on par with its critical access peers, showing that a small rural hospital can move the measures VBC contracts reward with simple, disciplined transition steps.
set.source: Copley Hospital, Community Health Needs Assessment Progress Report 2018 (Green Mountain Care Board hospital budget filing B19H31)

ops.claim: Copley: OneCare member; RN follows every discharge for 30 days; risk tool; readmissions 'well below state and national averages' (DVHA All-Payer Model evaluation)
ops.note: Program details and the cited DVHA evaluation could not be found; replaced with Copley's own documented actions and rates.
